topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and establishes the learning outcomes for this lecture.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains cancer development as the stepwise accumulation of changes affecting cellular genes and their regulation.

topics.label: Cancer as disrupted differentiation and tissue organization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why understanding cancer requires attention to the organized tissue context that isolated cell cultures cannot fully reproduce.

topics.label: Invasion and metastasis as features of malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how malignant tumors breach their local boundaries and spread, contrasting their behavior with contained benign growth.

topics.label: Progression and clinical significance of benign tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the possible outcomes of benign tumor growth, showing through colorectal progression that malignancy can develop but is neither inevitable nor necessary for harm.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor names communicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor growth disrupts normal bodily function and produces potentially fatal disease.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence of tumor types across populations and species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how screening addresses the difficulty of detecting cancer early and why its effectiveness varies between tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture close and follow-up
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students toward revision and upcoming practicals.
